title: Bug: wait_until does not properly handle exceptions raised by failed pytest_assert
author: wrideout-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Low

### Description of the bug

Found while debugging a different issue:

  - pytest_assert (tests/common/helpers/assertions.py) calls pytest.fail() on
    failure.
  - pytest.fail() raises _pytest.outcomes.Failed, which inherits from
    OutcomeException -> BaseException (NOT Exception).
  - wait_until (tests/common/utilities.py:125) catches only `except Exception`,
    so Failed propagates straight through and aborts the test on the first
    attempt.
  - The wait_until window is therefore effectively dead for mismatch cases.
    Only genuine Exception subclasses are handled correctly and get retried.

The fix appears to be to use a more targeted try/except handler here: 

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/common/utilities.py#L151

### Steps to Reproduce

This was found while debugging generic_config_updater/test_dynamic_acl.py.  In the case I was investigating, the status output of `show acl table DYNAMIC_ACL` was initially reported as "NA".  This was causing the wait_until wrapping the check to be skipped and the test to be failed outright.

Lib in question is here:

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/common/gu_utils.py#L531

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Failures due to pytest_assert invoked from within a wait_until should not cause an immediate test failure (as they do today).  The exception should be handled and the retry mechanism continued.

comments.author: rbpittman
comments.body: Seems to me that some use-cases expect failures to occur (this issue's use-case), whereas others do not expect exceptions. In these latter use-cases I mention (QOS-related), an exception in the function passed to wait_until really needs to be reported, and can mask bad issues. Wonder if it's appropriate to extend wait_until to support skipping the exception checker too.

comments.author: wrideout-arista
comments.body: Instead of skipping the try/except, we could allow wait_until to raise an exception once the iteration/time condition is met and achieve the same thing, no?

comments.author: wrideout-arista
comments.body:
> Instead of skipping the try/except, we could allow wait_until to raise an exception once the iteration/time condition is met and achieve the same thing, no?

I take that back: in the overwhelming majority of cases raising an exception will break the common pattern of using wait_until inside an enclosing pytest_assert.

On it's face, it appears to me that the above is als true if the exception handling is skipped.  In that case maybe a new method, "wait_until_and_raise_exception" or similar is more appropriate?

comments.author: rbpittman
comments.body:
Sure, or alternatively a parameter "raise_exception" that defaults to False, and can be overridden to true. 

But yes that's somewhat tangential to your issue, sounds appropriate to properly catch all exceptions since that's the expectation in most cases.

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
wait_until already handles Exception, and multiple places in the code assume pytest.fail.Exception is handled as well.  pytest.fail.Exception actually derives from BaseException, which means it is currently unhandled by wait_until, and so will not trigger retries (and immediately fail tests).

#### How did you do it?
Added pytest.fail.Exception to the list of handled exception classes in wait_until.

comments.author: bhouse-nexthop
comments.body: Review notes (seeking a second opinion): the fix is correct — `pytest.fail.Exception` derives from `BaseException`, so it escapes the current `except Exception` in `wait_until`. But this changes `wait_until` behavior **repo-wide**: a `pytest_assert`/`pytest.fail` raised inside any `wait_until` condition is now swallowed and retried until timeout instead of failing fast. That's the intended fix, but it could change behavior for existing call sites that relied on fast-fail. Given the blast radius on a shared helper, we'd like a common-infra maintainer's sign-off — @wangxin @lolyu, could one of you weigh in on the `wait_until` semantics change? (Also: title typo, "Exeption".)

comments.author: anders-nexthop
comments.body:
Building on @bhouse-nexthop's blast-radius question, I ran a repo-wide audit, since the failure-mode flip only matters for `wait_until` conditions that can actually raise `pytest.fail.Exception`. I resolved each `wait_until` condition to its definition (local def first, then imports) and checked whether it calls `pytest_assert`/`pytest.fail`.

Of ~1,570 `wait_until` call sites, the large majority pass a bool-returning condition and are unaffected — including the high-frequency ones (`critical_services_fully_started`, `check_bgp_session_state`, `is_service_fully_started`, ...), none of which assert. About 22 sites pass a condition that asserts internally, and for those the deciding factor is whether the call site uses `wait_until`'s return:

- Return asserted (`pytest_assert(wait_until(...), msg)`): after this change a failing inner assert still fails the test, just with a vaguer message after the full timeout — and a transient guard-trip (DB row not populated yet, a `docker exec` hiccup during a restart) now retries through instead of fast-failing. That is the improvement this PR is after, and it covers most of the 22. No concern.
- Return ignored (bare `wait_until(...)`): today the inner assert is the only failure mechanism. After this change it is swallowed, retried, and the `False` return is discarded — so the check becomes a silent no-op that can never fail. These are the ones worth fixing alongside this change.

The return-ignored sites I found — 3 functions, 4 call sites:

| call site | condition | effect after this PR |
|-----------|-----------|----------------------|
| `tests/common/gu_utils.py` (`check_table`) | returns False until the ACL table populates, then `pytest_assert`s its content | a GCU ACL content mismatch is silently ignored instead of failing |
| `tests/monit/test_monit_status.py` + `tests/bmp/test_frr_bmp_sanity.py` (`check_monit_expected_container_logging`) | body is only `pytest_assert(...)`, returns None | both calls become ~180s no-ops that can never fail |
| `tests/show_techsupport/test_techsupport.py` (`execute_command`) | `pytest.fail`s on a techsupport failure, return discarded; the next line reads `pytest.tar_stdout` | a real failure is swallowed (and the expensive command retried for the full 300s), then downstream hits stale/unset `pytest.tar_stdout` |

Suggestion: the `wait_until` change is the right direction — keep it, but land it together with converting those 4 sites so they no longer rely on the assert escaping (have the condition return a bool and assert `wait_until`'s result, e.g. wrap the asserting helper). Re-raising from `wait_until` on final timeout would be an alternative, but that changes the contract for the ~1000 callers that rely on the `False`-on-timeout return, so per-site fixes look safer.

Happy to share the full call-site list or the script I used.

*— anders-bot (AI-assisted, on behalf of @anders-nexthop)*
